--ui-color-page.projectOverride: No global page-background override. apps/mintaka/theme/themeConfig.ts currently provides token: {}.
--ui-color-page.notes: Panda colorBgLayout is a layout surface and does not equal the Catalog white page. Keep the canvas layout-owned until a product-wide theme decision exists.

--ui-color-card.projectOverride: Panda generated default in components/theme/themes/shared/genColorMapToken.ts; no app override.
--ui-color-card.notes: Exact white card and focused-surface token.

--ui-color-title.projectOverride: Panda generated default; apps/alnitak TeacherIntro TAB_THEME applies the same value to Tabs only.
--ui-color-title.notes: Exact strong-title token. Use it for headings and other confirmed strong text roles.

--ui-color-text.projectOverride: Panda generated default; ProfileSettingsClient has a scoped legacy colorText override with the same value.

--ui-color-secondary.projectOverride: No application override. Panda default is #9C9CAC, not the Catalog #767687.
--ui-color-secondary.notes: Use a reviewed ConfigProvider theme override only where secondary text must match Catalog; do not substitute the placeholder token.

--ui-color-placeholder.projectOverride: Panda generated default in components/theme/themes/shared/genColorMapToken.ts; no app override.

--ui-color-disabled.projectOverride: No application override for the Catalog #C7CBD3 disabled text value.
--ui-color-disabled.notes: Panda exposes the semantic disabled token, but its current derived value is not the Catalog value. In ConfigProvider, set colorTextQuaternary because colorTextDisabled is derived from it.

--ui-color-border.projectOverride: Panda generated default in components/theme/themes/shared/genColorMapToken.ts; no app override.
--ui-color-border.notes: Exact default input and component boundary token.

--ui-color-divider.projectOverride: Panda generated default in components/theme/themes/shared/genColorMapToken.ts; no app override.
--ui-color-divider.notes: Exact quiet internal divider and light fill token.

--ui-color-hover.projectOverride: No application override for the Catalog #EBEDF1 hover surface.
--ui-color-hover.notes: Panda exposes a hover-fill token, but its generated default differs from Catalog. In ConfigProvider, set colorFill because colorFillContentHover is derived from it.

--ui-color-primary.projectOverride: Panda generated default is #FF4438; no application override aligns it to the Catalog #FF4338.
--ui-color-primary.notes: Use the custom Panda primary-main token for red CTA behavior; a reviewed theme override is required for the exact Catalog value.

--ui-color-primary-hover.projectOverride: Panda generated default in components/theme/themes/shared/genColorMapToken.ts; no app override.
--ui-color-primary-hover.notes: Exact red hover, pressed, and destructive color.

--ui-color-primary-shade-1.projectOverride: Panda generated default is #FF7B73, not the Catalog #FF8E87.
--ui-color-primary-shade-1.notes: Use an explicit reviewed override for the lower-priority warm accent.

--ui-color-link.projectOverride: No application override. Panda derives its link color from the info seed by default.
--ui-color-link.notes: Panda supports the semantic link token, but it must be overridden to the Catalog #59779A.

--ui-color-link-hover.projectOverride: No application override for the Catalog #4B647D link hover value.
--ui-color-link-hover.notes: Set only alongside the approved link theme decision; do not derive an arbitrary darker color locally.

--ui-color-info.projectOverride: Panda seed default in components/theme/themes/seed.ts; no app override.

--ui-color-info-surface.projectOverride: No application override for the Catalog #EDFAFA information surface.
--ui-color-info-surface.notes: Panda supports the semantic information background but its generated value must be verified or overridden.

--ui-color-accessory-1.projectOverride: No application override for the Catalog #FFF9E6 warning-derived accessory surface.
--ui-color-accessory-1.notes: Use only where the Catalog role is warning-related; otherwise retain it as a local approved accessory surface.

--ui-color-accessory-2.projectOverride: No Panda semantic token or application override represents this #E6F7F8 decorative accessory surface.
--ui-color-accessory-2.notes: Do not replace it with colorInfoBg without an approved semantic decision.

--ui-color-accessory-3.projectOverride: Panda generated default in components/theme/themes/shared/genColorMapToken.ts; no app override.

--ui-color-accessory-4.projectOverride: No Panda semantic token or application override represents this #E7FCF5 accessory surface.
--ui-color-accessory-4.notes: Do not treat an accessory color as Panda success without an approved semantic decision.

--ui-color-available.projectOverride: No Panda availability token or product-wide availability theme override exists.
--ui-color-available.notes: Availability is a booking-domain state, not a substitute for Panda success.

--ui-color-available-surface.projectOverride: No Panda availability-surface token or product-wide availability theme override exists.
--ui-color-available-surface.notes: Keep this as a Calendar or booking adapter token until an availability theme contract is approved.

--ui-color-available-current-day-surface.projectOverride: No Panda current-availability-day token or product-wide availability theme override exists.
--ui-color-available-current-day-surface.notes: Calendar current-day availability remains a documented booking adapter concern.

--ui-color-success.projectOverride: Panda seed default in components/theme/themes/seed.ts; no app override.

--ui-color-success-surface.projectOverride: No application override for the Catalog #ECFFF9 success surface.
--ui-color-success-surface.notes: Panda supports the semantic success background but its generated value must be verified or overridden.

--ui-color-warning.projectOverride: Panda seed default in components/theme/themes/seed.ts; no app override.

--ui-color-warning-surface.projectOverride: No application override for the Catalog #FFF9E6 warning surface.
--ui-color-warning-surface.notes: Panda supports the semantic warning background but its generated value must be verified or overridden.

--ui-color-error.projectOverride: Panda seed default in components/theme/themes/seed.ts; no app override.

--ui-color-error-surface.projectOverride: No application override for the Catalog #FFF1F1 error surface.
--ui-color-error-surface.notes: Use the semantic error background token only after its value is aligned through a reviewed theme decision.

--ui-color-on-primary.projectOverride: Panda generated default resolves to colorWhite; no app override.

--ui-color-modal-mask.projectOverride: No application override. Panda default is a 45% black mask, not the Catalog title-color 24% mask.
--ui-color-modal-mask.notes: Use the semantic mask token only with an approved overlay theme override.

--ui-color-upload-overlay.projectOverride: No global Panda token or project override defines the Catalog upload overlay alpha.
--ui-color-upload-overlay.notes: This is Upload-specific feedback treatment and requires an approved component-level token or adapter.

--ui-color-upload-loading.projectOverride: No global Panda token or project override defines the Catalog upload loading alpha.
--ui-color-upload-loading.notes: This is Upload-specific loading treatment and requires an approved component-level token or adapter.

--ui-color-on-primary-muted.projectOverride: No Panda semantic token or project override represents this 45% white content treatment.
--ui-color-on-primary-muted.notes: Do not approximate with disabled text; it is contextual on-color content.

--ui-color-on-emphasis-muted.projectOverride: No Panda semantic token or project override represents this 55% white content treatment.
--ui-color-on-emphasis-muted.notes: Do not approximate with disabled text; it is contextual on-emphasis content.

--ui-color-emphasis-weak.projectOverride: No Panda semantic token or project override represents this title-color alpha treatment.
--ui-color-emphasis-weak.notes: This requires an approved component-level treatment rather than a generic Panda color substitution.

--ui-color-disabled-weak.projectOverride: No Panda semantic token or project override represents this disabled alpha treatment.
--ui-color-disabled-weak.notes: This requires an approved component-level treatment rather than a generic Panda color substitution.

--ui-color-hover-overlay.projectOverride: No Panda semantic token or project override represents this title-color hover overlay.
--ui-color-hover-overlay.notes: Use only through a reviewed component interaction token; do not replace it with an arbitrary grey.

statusDefinitions.direct: The Catalog prop has a confirmed Panda prop or native attribute destination.
statusDefinitions.adapter: The value is supported only through a documented Panda composition or product adapter.
statusDefinitions.catalog-only: The prop controls a Catalog fixture or example state and must not be copied into production code.
statusDefinitions.gap: No confirmed Panda API safely represents this Catalog prop. Report the gap instead of styling around it.

button.notes: Use the product wrapper. Catalog variants are not a second Button API; resolve the variant through this map before implementation.

label.notes: Pass the visible button label as children.

variant.pandaProp: type | text | outlined | special | ghost | danger
variant.notes: Map each Catalog variant through the approved product convention. Confirm ghost, danger, plus, and emphasis visuals before use; do not infer them from another library.

size.notes: Panda uses semantic sizes rather than Catalog pixel values. The application adapter owns the 32/40/48 mapping.

shape.notes: Panda supports default, circle, and round. Resolve Catalog rounded and pill values through the product wrapper.

state.notes: The Catalog fixture displays interaction states; Panda derives them from behavior and props.

leadingIcon.notes: Panda Button renders its icon before children.

trailingIcon.notes: Panda has no dedicated trailing-icon prop. Use an approved content composition without changing Button anatomy.

iconOnly.notes: Use the Panda icon path with an accessible name; this is not an independent Boolean Panda prop.

ariaLabel.notes: Native ARIA attribute forwarded by Button.

href.notes: Panda renders the supported link form.

download.notes: Native anchor attribute supported by the link form.

target.notes: Native anchor attribute supported by the link form.

rel.notes: Native anchor attribute supported by the link form.

ariaExpanded.notes: Native ARIA attribute forwarded by Button.

ariaPressed.notes: Native ARIA attribute forwarded by Button.

ariaDescribedBy.notes: Native ARIA attribute forwarded by Button.

ariaControls.notes: Native ARIA attribute forwarded by Button.

checkbox.notes: Use Checkbox for semantic multi-select choices. Group handling belongs to Checkbox.Group.

state.notes: Fixture interaction state; not a Panda prop.

toggleMode.notes: Binary, mixed, and controlled modes describe usage patterns rather than one Panda prop.

checkbox-group.notes: Use the Group for controlled multi-select values. Labels, validation, and select-all are composed concerns.

id.notes: Choose the accessible field identifier in the Form/fieldset adapter.

options.notes: Use Panda option objects with label, value, and optional disabled state.

layout.notes: Panda Group does not expose a vertical/inline layout prop.

selectAll.notes: Derive select-all and mixed state in the product adapter.

feedback.notes: Validation copy belongs to the field wrapper.

feedbackTone.notes: Resolve semantic feedback tone through Form.Item.

radio.notes: Use Radio for one-of-many choices and Radio.Group for controlled group state.

state.notes: Fixture interaction state; not a Panda prop.

description.notes: Panda Radio has no dedicated description prop.

tabIndex.notes: Native focus-order attribute supported by Radio.

modal.notes: Modal trigger ownership and lifecycle live in the calling feature. Use the existing reviewed modal flow.

id.notes: Modal has no top-level id prop; assign identifiers in a reviewed accessibility wrapper.

trigger.notes: Panda Modal does not own its trigger.

triggerLabel.notes: The trigger label belongs to the invoking control.

size.notes: Map Catalog 520/744 sizes to the verified Panda width value.

titleAlign.notes: No semantic alignment prop exists; do not add local modal CSS.

search.notes: Panda owns the field surface; query timing, suggestions, results, and route synchronization remain feature behavior.

value.notes: Controlled search value; the feature supplies onChange.

size.notes: Resolve Catalog pixel size to Panda semantic size in the product adapter.

shape.notes: Panda Input.Search has no confirmed semantic rounded/pill API. Do not add an ad-hoc class.

state.notes: Fixture interaction state; not a Panda prop.

select.notes: Use Panda Select for selection mechanics. Remote query, option data, labels, and filtering remain feature-owned.

id.notes: Identifier forwarded to the select control.

label.notes: Select does not own a separate visible field label.

options.notes: Use Panda option records with supported labels, values, and disabled state.

groups.notes: Translate Catalog groups to Panda's nested option structure.

mode.notes: Catalog single means omit mode; multiple maps to Panda mode=multiple.

size.notes: Resolve Catalog pixel size to Panda semantic size in the product adapter.

shape.notes: Panda Select has no confirmed semantic rounded/pill API. Do not add an ad-hoc class.

status.notes: Use Panda warning or error input status.

state.notes: Fixture interaction state; loading and open have their own Panda props.

query.notes: Controlled search text requires feature query handling and should be used with showSearch.

drawer.notes: Drawer trigger ownership and lifecycle live in the calling feature. Use the existing reviewed drawer flow.

id.notes: Drawer has no top-level id prop for the Catalog fixture identifier.

trigger.notes: Panda Drawer does not own its trigger.

triggerLabel.notes: The trigger label belongs to the invoking control.

size.notes: Panda provides default/large plus explicit width and height. Resolve Catalog default/wide per direction in the product adapter.

form-field.notes: Form.Item owns labels, help, validation, and required state around a supported control. Field control shape remains a component decision.

control.notes: Place the supported Panda control in Form.Item children.

error.notes: Error text needs both Panda validation state and help content.

size.pandaProp: Form size or child control size
size.notes: Form.Item does not translate Catalog pixels; resolve the supported control's size in the field adapter.

shape.notes: Form.Item has no shape API. Do not style the wrapper to mimic Catalog shapes.

state.notes: Fixture interaction state; control behavior owns focus and hover.

required.notes: Use Panda required marker behavior; validation rules remain feature-owned.

disabled.notes: Choose the correct scope in the form adapter; Form.Item itself has no disabled prop.

text-input.notes: Use Panda Input for text entry and keep controlled value lifecycle in the calling feature.

value.notes: Controlled input value; the feature supplies onChange.

size.notes: Resolve Catalog pixel size to Panda semantic size in the product adapter.

shape.notes: Panda Input has no confirmed semantic rounded/pill API. Do not add an ad-hoc class.

status.notes: Use Panda warning or error input status.

state.notes: Fixture interaction state; not a Panda prop.

trailingAction.notes: Choose the approved slot based on whether the action belongs inside or after the field.

ariaLabel.notes: Native ARIA attribute forwarded to Input.

textarea.notes: Use Panda Input.TextArea for multiline entry and keep controlled value lifecycle in the calling feature.

value.notes: Controlled textarea value; the feature supplies onChange.

size.notes: Resolve Catalog pixel size to Panda semantic size in the product adapter.

status.notes: Use Panda warning or error input status.

state.notes: Fixture interaction state; not a Panda prop.

ariaLabel.notes: Native ARIA attribute forwarded to TextArea.

toast.notes: Panda message is an imperative transient-feedback API, not a mounted Toast component. Use a reviewed notification lifecycle.

tone.notes: Use Panda info, success, warning, or error type.

title.notes: Message has one content node; compose the title using an approved toast content pattern.

description.notes: Message has no description slot; compose content only through an approved pattern.

action.notes: Message has no action slot; recovery actions require an approved content pattern.

closable.notes: Panda message ArgsProps has no close-icon prop. Do not fabricate one inside the message surface.

open.notes: Opening is an imperative lifecycle call rather than a React prop.

ariaLabel.notes: Panda message ArgsProps has no confirmed aria-label prop. Preserve accessible feedback through the approved message API.

notification.notes: Panda notification is an imperative feedback API. Use an approved feature lifecycle and recovery action boundary.

tone.notes: Use Panda info, success, warning, or error type.

closable.notes: Use Panda close icon behavior, including false when the approved flow must not dismiss.

open.notes: Opening is an imperative lifecycle call rather than a React prop.

ariaLabel.notes: Panda accepts native div props through the nested props object.

button.notes: Use the existing Panda wrapper. Do not recreate button anatomy or translate Catalog variants directly without checking Panda props.

chip.notes: Panda Chip does not cover the Catalog 24px geometry or semantic button behavior. Use the React design-system adapter; never use Chip as a checkbox or radio replacement.

link.notes: New to the kit, with no upstream equivalent to adapt. The Foundation already carried Color/Link and the Link/16 and Link/14 typography tiers, and the teacher card was hand-rolling both; this is the component those specs describe. Not a substitute for Button: a Link goes somewhere, a Button does something.

tag.notes: Panda Tag does not guarantee the Catalog close affordance, size scale, or semantic tones. Use the React design-system adapter for compact descriptive labels.

checkbox.notes: Use Panda Checkbox for semantic multi-select choices and its documented group API.

checkbox-group.notes: Use Panda Checkbox.Group for controlled groups; product-specific option data and validation remain outside the primitive.

radio.notes: Use Panda Radio or Radio.Group for one-of-many choices rather than custom selected rows.

selection.notes: Panda Selection does not cover the Catalog content types, selected marker, or radio and checkbox semantics. Use the React design-system adapter; use standalone Radio or Checkbox when a compact control is sufficient.

date-picker.notes: Use the React design-system adapter for Catalog size, shape, field status, controlled or uncontrolled opening, single or range selection, month navigation, and disabled days with YYYY-MM-DD values. Booking availability and timezone policy remain product concerns.

tooltip.notes: Use the React design-system adapter for placement, arrowless mode, focus behavior, and delayed hover presentation; do not make a Tooltip the only access path to essential content.

modal.notes: Use the Panda wrapper and an existing reviewed modal flow. Confirm focus restoration and custom footer behavior before extending it.

popup.notes: Use the React design-system adapter for Catalog-owned trigger modes, placement, outside dismissal, Escape behavior, and leave delay. Do not use Popup as an unreviewed menu or modal substitute.

popconfirm.notes: Use the React design-system adapter for a local consequential action, controlled or uncontrolled open state, outside dismissal, Escape behavior, loading, and confirmation callbacks.

divider.notes: Use the existing Panda wrapper for structural separation and labelled dividers.

avatar.notes: Use the React design-system adapter for the Catalog size scale, image fallback, flag placement, logo treatment, and avatar-group overlap. Panda remains an internal implementation option, not the product import boundary.

badge.notes: Use the React design-system adapter for Catalog count, dot, status, overflow, and anchor behavior. Panda remains an internal implementation option, not the product import boundary.

breadcrumb.notes: Use the React design-system adapter for collapsed overflow, current-page semantics, and Catalog separator behavior. Page routing remains product-owned.

card.notes: Use the React design-system adapter for the Catalog surface, media-ratio, density, and interactive-card contract. Business objects such as teacher cards remain composed product patterns.

alert.notes: Use the Panda wrapper for persistent in-context feedback, not field validation or transient notification behavior.

tabs.notes: Use the React design-system adapter for Catalog labels, count treatment, trailing action, and automatic or manual keyboard activation.

pagination.notes: Use the React design-system adapter for supplied page lists, ellipsis treatment, controlled current page, and disabled boundary actions. Page fetches, route state, and total-result semantics stay product-owned.

rate.notes: Use the React design-system adapter for Catalog half-step, clearable, preview, label, and keyboard rating behavior. Do not calculate rating aggregates in the component.

sidebar.notes: Use the React design-system Sidebar for controlled or local collapse, Pin and More movement, same-list drag ordering, bounded More disclosure, section animation, and internal smooth scrolling. Product adapters still supply destinations, state, approved icons, persistence, route behavior, and analytics.

statistic.notes: Use the React design-system adapter for supplied values, affixes, descriptions, and loading presentation. Formatting and calculation remain product-owned.

table.notes: Use the React design-system adapter for supplied columns, row headers, compact density, loading, empty state, and responsive overflow. Sorting, pagination, and selection remain product-owned.

timeline.notes: Use the React design-system adapter for supplied event history, semantic dot tones, pending state, labels, reverse order, and alternate layout. Event meaning remains caller-owned.

top-nav.notes: Use the React design-system TopNav, TopNavContext, and TopNavSearch for its three-slot 72px shell, centred search expansion, language/context menu, and reviewed icon geometry. Product adapters still supply navigation meaning, query effects, language state, account actions, routes, and analytics.

slider.notes: Use the React design-system adapter for single, range, vertical, reverse, disabled, tooltip, and controlled slider presentation. Domain values and validation remain product behavior.

panel.notes: Use the React design-system adapter for a titled content surface, supplied extra action, density, and optional structural divider. Avoid decorative nested cards.

search.notes: Use Panda Input.Search for the field surface. Query timing, suggestions, results, and route synchronization require product behavior.

select.notes: Use the Panda wrapper for confirmed selection behavior; option data, remote search, and business filters remain product-owned.

switch.notes: Use the React design-system adapter for immediate binary changes, semantic switch behavior, and the Catalog 44px control geometry. Persistence and confirmation remain caller-owned.

drawer.notes: Use the Panda wrapper with an existing reviewed drawer flow; route, focus, dismissal, and responsive content behavior must be verified.

form-field.notes: Use Panda Form.Item for labels, help text, validation display, and required state around supported controls.

text-input.notes: Use the Panda wrapper for text entry. Prefix, suffix, validation, and controlled value behavior must follow the current API.

textarea.notes: Use Panda Input.TextArea for multiline entry and rely on its verified count, read-only, and status behavior.

number-stepper.notes: Use the React design-system adapter for Catalog size, shape, bounds, increment controls, and controlled numeric entry. Unit semantics and validation messages remain product behavior.

combobox.notes: Use the React design-system adapter for searchable single selection, query, loading, option groups, size, shape, and status. Fetching, ranking, and query policy remain product behavior.

upload.notes: Use the React design-system adapter for dropzone, trigger, avatar upload, local file list presentation, remove actions, complete/uploading/error states, and client-side selection. Upload targets, validation policy, server progress, and file lifecycle remain product-owned.

stepper.notes: Use the React design-system adapter for default and flow-progress step anatomy, orientation, current state, disabled steps, and controlled navigation. Completion rules remain in the flow adapter.

progress.notes: Use the React design-system adapter for supplied progress values, default/success/error status, indeterminate loading, and accessible progress semantics. Completion meaning remains product-owned.

toast.notes: Use Panda message for transient feedback. Application context, queueing, duration, and recovery actions must follow a reviewed product pattern.

notification.notes: Use the Panda notification API for persistent transient feedback and keep product outcomes and actions in the caller.

result.notes: Use Panda Result for terminal or recoverable outcome presentation; the next action remains a product decision.

skeleton.notes: Use the React design-system adapter for Catalog text, content, avatar, button, input, image, and card placeholders. It honors reduced motion; do not use it to hide missing required content.

dropdown-menu.notes: Use the React design-system adapter for menu placement, open state, icon sizing, disabled and destructive items, and keyboard dismissal. Item meaning, permissions, and analytics remain product behavior.

disclosure.notes: Use the React design-system adapter for accordion/details anatomy, open state, disabled behavior, and the approved 24px disclosure icon.

segmented-control.notes: Use the React design-system adapter for the Catalog 32/40/48 geometry, rounded or pill shape, and immediate selected-mode state.

time-slot.notes: Use the React design-system primitive for availability and option appearances, booking locks, duration, selected state, loading, and delayed tooltips. Booking permissions and availability data remain product behavior.

time-picker.notes: Use the React design-system adapter for controlled or uncontrolled open state, option-grid sizing, TimeSlot presentation, selected values, disabled state, and Escape/outside dismissal. Availability, timezone, and bookable-duration rules remain product-owned.

calendar.notes: Use the React design-system adapter for availability, teacher availability, compact availability, and lesson record views. It owns responsive day columns, sticky date headers, scrollable time areas, TimeSlot state, one-hour selection from 15-minute cells, week/date switching, and tooltip placement. Availability data, booking policy, timezone conversion, and lesson history retrieval remain product behavior.

footer.notes: Use the React design-system Footer for its reviewed layout and accessible link groups. Footer links, locale, legal copy, social destinations, and utility controls remain product-supplied content.

popover.notes: Use the React design-system adapter for reviewed contextual floating content. It shares Popup placement, trigger, dismissal, and hover-delay behavior; keep trigger meaning and actions in the caller.
